b: n-of-many: A new study details a strategy to scale up genetic therapies that have, to date, only been tested in n-of-1 trials. Antisense oligonucleotides were custom-made for two people with SCN2A-complex neurodevelopmental disorder, a severe childhood-onset condition that can result in autism and epileptic encephalopathy. Gene-specific haplotyping enabled researchers to identify additional people with compatible diplotypes. The investigators envision prequalifying a small set of antisense oligonucleotides that target the most common SCN2A causal variants. The Transmitter has previously covered the promise and concerns over n-of-1 trials.
